objects.name: Support (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
A support. Rigid: fixes the node along and about the axes of the Position's plane you choose. Elastic: a spring along or about each axis of the plane. Compression Only: holds the node only while it pushes into the support, along the plane's Z, and lets it lift - after a gap, if there is one.
Elastic and Compression Only never fix the node themselves, so a Rigid support on the same point can hold what they leave free: a pinned bearing that can lift is a Compression Only support with a Rigid one holding Tx and Ty only.
Reaction Force gives a spring support a row of its own, with the spring's force.

objects.name: Section Optimiser (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Sizes beams from lists of sections. It analyses the model, checks every beam that takes part with every section of its list on the forces the beam carried - EN 1993-1-1, as Utilisation does - puts it on the first section of the list that keeps its utilisation at or below MaxUtilisation, and analyses again, as the new sections change the self-weight and, in a statically indeterminate structure, where the forces go. It stops when no section changes, or after Iterations analyses.
A beam's list is its Design Group's, in the order given: the group's beams all take one section, or, with its Uniform off, each its own. A beam in no group is sized within the family of the section it starts with in Section Library - an HEA200 among the HEAs, a CHS among the CHS - smallest area first; a section that is not from Section Library has no family, and keeps its place.
Every beam takes part unless ElementId says which. Those left out keep their sections, and are still checked.
A beam can move back up its list as well as down it. When a design comes round again the iterations after it only let beams move on down their lists, which ends.
Each analysis is static, in one step. Buckling lengths, fabrication and partial factors are in the Design menu, the solver in the Analysis menu. Steel only, as the check is. Press Escape to stop after the iteration under way.

objects.name: Model View (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc:
Draw the model and its results in the viewport.
Tick one or more results under Results - displacements, beam forces and stresses, shell forces and stresses, solid stresses, reactions - to draw them together, each with its own component and unit. Under Beam forces, tick any of N, Vy, Vz, T, My and Mz to draw their diagrams together. They need a model from Run Analysis or another analysis. Each element is coloured by one result: an element's own stress or force before the displacement, which colours the rest.
With none ticked, the elements are coloured by element, section or material.
Node and element ids, section names, local axes, end releases, loads and supports can be drawn over either, from the Elements, Loads and Supports menus.
ElementId shows only some of the elements and greys the rest, so what you are looking at stays in the model around it.
Geometry hands out what is drawn as coloured meshes and lines - move it, or bake it.
With Extruded on, beam stresses that differ across a section - σx, σMy, σMz, τV, τT, Von Mises - are painted point by point over it; drawn as lines, each section shows its worst.
A vibration or buckling mode is drawn at deformation scale 1 with its largest movement as far off the model as the diagrams stand; any other displacement at true size. On a natural vibration or buckling model the scale runs from -2 to 2, so Animate swings the mode both ways.

objects.name: Design Group (Alpaca4d)
objects.desc: Beams that the Section Optimiser sizes from one list of sections: the beams with these ElementIds, and the sections they may be. Uniform, the whole group takes the first section of the list, in the order given, that every one of its beams can carry its forces with: give a member drawn as several beams a group of its own, so that it ends up with one section, as it will be built. With Uniform off, each beam takes the first section of the list that it can carry its forces with.

objects.name: Panel
objects.desc: A panel for custom notes and text values
objects.text:
Curved beam - a Section Optimiser example.

A 12 m beam curves up and down in a vertical plane. It is built in at its start, held up at 15% and 33% of the way along, and free beyond: a continuous beam ending in a long cantilever, with 50 kN hanging near its far end and its own weight. It is cut into 30 elements, IPE300 in S355 to begin with.

6 - Each element on its own. No design group: each element goes to the first section of the family it starts in - the IPEs for an IPE300 - that keeps it at or below MaxUtilisation, smallest area first. The beam grows over the third support, where the cantilever's moment is largest, and thins out towards the load and the built-in start. Switch the starting section to HEA300 and it stays among the HEAs.

7 - One section for the whole beam: a design group over every element, from the list of IPEs in the panel, tried in the order it gives them.

Reshape the curve in the two panels of 2, and move the supports and the load with their sliders: each lands on the node nearest the fraction given. The top flange is held sideways every 0.5 m, wired into LengthLT in the Design menu; sized element by element, an unrestrained beam is only a rough guide, as lateral-torsional buckling belongs to the whole member.
